title: Cherry Frangipane Tart
changes_from_base: Fresh cherries pressed into a processor frangipane made from flaked almonds, in place of poached pears.
summary: Sweet cherries pressed into a creamy almond frangipane in a crisp short pastry case.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
chilled unsalted butter, in small pieces
large egg yolk, beaten with 2 tsp water
flaked almonds, plus 15 g for the top

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: mix the flour, sugar and salt, rub in the butter completely, then stir in the yolk and water. Knead briefly until smooth and flatten into a disc.

steps.title: Line
steps.text: roll out to a 28 cm round, press it into the tin and patch any cracks with trimmings. Chill 1 h (or freeze).

steps.title: Bake the case
steps.text: heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Bake the case on the tray, uncovered and without beans, about 15 min, until lightly browned. No beans are needed; this pastry holds its shape.

steps.title: Frangipane
steps.text: meanwhile, grind the 110 g almonds with the flour and sugar to a coarse powder. Pulse in the butter, then add the eggs and almond extract and process about 2 min, until smooth and creamy.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: spread the frangipane in the hot case and press the cherries into it in one layer. Scatter over the extra 15 g almonds.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: turn the oven down to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and bake 30-40 min, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Check with a skewer between the cherries, not into one.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: cool on the rack, remove the ring and dust with icing sugar.

tips: A cherry stoner saves a lot of time.
Frozen pitted cherries work; thaw and pat them dry.
Ground almonds (110 g) can replace the flaked almonds; mix the filling by hand.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 2 days.
